items.title: Mozambique named Best Tourism Investment Destination at World Tourism Awards 2026
items.summary: Photo: World Tourism Forum Institute The award marks a second consecutive year of recognition for Mozambique at the World Tourism Awards, following its selection as Best Sustainable Destination in 2025. Together, the two honours tell a clear story: a country long admired for its coastline, islands and wildlife is now also earning the confidence of international investors Tourism at the heart of a new economic vision Since taking office in January 2025, President Daniel Francisco Chapo has placed tourism at the centre of Mozambique’s economic agenda. He presents the sector as a strategic engine of growth, jobs and social inclusion, and as the surest path to diversifying the economy beyond natural gas, coal and other extractive resources. “Gas will one day run out… tourism will never run out,” the President said earlier this month The Government’s Five-Year Programme for 2025–2029 turns that conviction into concrete targets raising tourism’s contribution to GDP to 6% by 2029 Reforms that open the door to investors The President’s vision has been matched by structural reform.

items.title: Mozambique and Portugal set to expand cooperation
items.summary: The announcement was made following a meeting between Mozambican President Daniel Chapo and the Portuguese Parliament’s Speaker, who is visiting the country Photo: Presidência da República de Moçambique Photo: Presidência da República de Moçambique Photo: Presidência da República de Moçambique Speaking to the press, Aguiar-Branco said the meeting had provided an opportunity to discuss various matters of common interest, with particular emphasis on deepening relations between the two countries and identifying new opportunities for cooperation In the parliamentary sphere, he highlighted the cooperation protocol signed on Monday at the Assembly of the Republic of Mozambique, which establishes new forms of collaboration between the two legislative bodies, particularly in the fields of digital technology and artificial intelligence During the meeting, Aguiar-Branco also conveyed to the Mozambican Head of State Portugal’s commitment to restoring peace in Cabo Delgado province, linking stability in the region to stronger economic relations and increased Portuguese investment in Mozambique…

items.title: Makers of GLP-1 drugs ordered to add warnings about rare eye condition that can lead to blindness
items.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) told makers of popular weight-loss GLP-1 drugs that they must add warning labels about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness Manufacturers of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and Zepbound must warn about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). The disorder happens when vessels supplying blood to the optic nerves become blocked, depriving the nerves of oxygen The condition can cause painless decreased vision in one eye, which can be permanent, the FDA said In a statement to the BBC, the American Academy of Ophthalmology said "any added risk appears small, and it has not been established that these medications cause NAION" "GLP-1 medications offer important benefits for people with diabetes, obesity, and heart disease, so our message to patients is simple," the group said. "Don't stop your medication without talking to your doctor, and if you notice sudden, painless vision loss in one eye, see an ophthalmologist promptly." There is no known treatment to reverse vision loss caused by NAION.

items.title: Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
items.summary: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations "We can no longer wait," declared Polish victims' organizations in a dramatic appeal to German civil society, published on November 5 on the website of the Foundation for Polish–German Reconciliation "Around 50,000 survivors of Nazi persecution during the German occupation still live in Poland today. They include former concentration camp and prison inmates, people deported to Germany for forced labor and those subjected to other forms of Nazi repression ," wrote the signatories of the appeal The open letter pointed out that many of the survivors are over 90 years old, struggling with illness and rising costs, and in need of help in their daily lives.

items.title: Meet the Peaky Blinders, Ukraine's drone unit protecting a devastated front-line city
items.summary: The BBC's Jonathan Beale reported from inside Slovyansk, one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control The town has become almost uninhabitable and has been under heavy bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs Members of a Ukrainian drone unit that call themselves Peaky Blinders, named after the cult BBC TV series, have taken on the task of intercepting Russian drones Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi

items.title: DR Congo: 66 soldiers sentenced to death for 'cowardice' in conflict with FRN rebels
items.summary: Dozens of defendants were put on trial over accusations that they abandoned their posts and refused to follow direct orders Some 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in DR Congo on charges of cowardice, mutiny, and failure to obey orders. The sentence was handed down by the Goma Garrison Military Court At least 71 members of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) were arrested in several separate incidents related to the fierce fighting between the military and rebel groups near the country's borders with Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi They were arrested on allegations of abandoning their posts or running away from clashes with FRN rebels. Prosecutors had sought capital punishment for 70 of the defendants, while asking for a 10-year jail term for an intelligence officer.
